issue.title: MavlinkDirect does not receive some messages via serial
issue.body:
I think I have found a bug in MavlinkDirect. The following MAVLink messages are (almost never) received when sent via a serial port, and subscribed to by MavlinkDirect:

```
HEARTBEAT 
SYS_STATUS
POWER_STATUS
MEMINFO
NAV_CONTROLLER_OUTPUT
MISSION_CURRENT
GPS_RAW_INT
```
There may be others, but these are the missing messages I've found so far in my testing.

Tested with MAVSDK version 3.15, installed from `libmavsdk-dev_3.15.0_debian12_arm64.deb`

### Test Code

I have two different C++ scripts/files that I am using for this testing:

* [mavlink_message_listener.cpp](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26691963/mavlink_message_listener.cpp) - uses `mavsdk.intercept_incoming_messages_async` to print out **every** MAVLink message on the device. This seems to work accurately as far as I can verify with QGroundControl/MissionPlanner. So I do trust this script, and it is actually heavily based on one of the mavsdk examples IIRC.
* [mavsdk_message_matrix.cpp](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26691988/mavsdk_message_matrix.cpp) - Iterates through a hard-coded list of MAVLink messages from both `serial:///dev/ttyUSB0:115200` and `udpin://192.168.1.6:14550` using BOTH **MavlinkDirect** and **MavlinkPassthrough**, then compiles a table of the results, populating it based on whether each message was received from that source. Full disclosure, this is a ChatGPT-generated script that is based off more basic scripts manually written by me, where I looked at each message one at a time. The result from this script matches what I have seen with my own, non-AI-generated scripts. I just wrote this script for convenience and to help you replicate my findings quickly.

### Expected Result:

I expect to see that every message is received (i.e. the message callback is called) for each message tested, regardless of whether it was subscribed to by MavlinkDirect OR MavlinkPassthrough, and regardless of the port used.

I have used mavlink_message_listener.cpp to verify that each message IS being sent to each UDP/serial port. 

### Actual Result:
This is the last part of the terminal output from mavsdk_message_matrix.cpp. It shows that there are seven message types that are NOT received by MavlinkDirect, but only when sent via serial. 

```
============================================================
Summary
============================================================

Message               | Direct  | Pass    | Direct  | Pass    |
----------------------| --------| --------| --------| --------|
                      | Serial  |         | UDP     |         |
----------------------| --------| --------| --------| --------|
GLOBAL_POSITION_INT   | YES     | YES     | YES     | YES     |
LOCAL_POSITION_NED    | YES     | YES     | YES     | YES     |
HEARTBEAT             | NO      | YES     | YES     | YES     |
SERVO_OUTPUT_RAW      | YES     | YES     | YES     | YES     |
RC_CHANNELS           | YES     | YES     | YES     | YES     |
COMMAND_ACK           | YES     | YES     | YES     | YES     |
AUTOPILOT_VERSION     | YES     | YES     | YES     | YES     |
SYS_STATUS            | NO      | YES     | YES     | YES     |
POWER_STATUS          | NO      | YES     | YES     | YES     |
MEMINFO               | NO      | YES     | YES     | YES     |
NAV_CONTROLLER_OUTPUT | NO      | YES     | YES     | YES     |
MISSION_CURRENT       | NO      | YES     | YES     | YES     |
GPS_RAW_INT           | NO      | YES     | YES     | YES     |
TIMESYNC              | YES     | YES     | YES     | YES     |
```
Just to reiterate, these missing messages ARE being sent to the serial port, as shown by this mavlink_message_listener.cpp output:
```
spsa:~/test_code/build$ ./Release/bin/MavlinkMessageListener serial:///dev/ttyUSB0:115200
[INFO] Setting up MAVLink listener...
[11:30:22|Info ] MAVSDK version: v3.15.0 (mavsdk_impl.cpp:33)
Connecting to serial:///dev/ttyUSB0:115200
[11:30:22|Debug] Component Autopilot (component ID: 1) added. (system_impl.cpp:496)
[11:30:22|Debug] Discovered 1 component (system_impl.cpp:616)
Connected to Generic running Unknown
[INFO] Listener running. Press Ctrl+C to stop.
SEQ: 191 SYS:   1 COMP:   1 MSGID:    33 | GLOBAL_POSITION_INT
SEQ: 192 SYS:   1 COMP:   1 MSGID:    32 | LOCAL_POSITION_NED
SEQ: 193 SYS:   1 COMP:   1 MSGID:    33 | GLOBAL_POSITION_INT
SEQ: 194 SYS:   1 COMP:   1 MSGID:    32 | LOCAL_POSITION_NED
SEQ: 196 SYS:   1 COMP:   0 MSGID:     0 | HEARTBEAT
SEQ: 195 SYS:   1 COMP:   1 MSGID:    36 | SERVO_OUTPUT_RAW
SEQ: 196 SYS:   1 COMP:   1 MSGID:    65 | RC_CHANNELS
SEQ: 197 SYS:   1 COMP:   1 MSGID:    33 | GLOBAL_POSITION_INT
SEQ: 198 SYS:   1 COMP:   1 MSGID:    32 | LOCAL_POSITION_NED
SEQ: 201 SYS:   1 COMP:   1 MSGID:    33 | GLOBAL_POSITION_INT
SEQ: 208 SYS:   1 COMP:   1 MSGID:    32 | LOCAL_POSITION_NED
SEQ: 209 SYS:   1 COMP:   1 MSGID:     0 | HEARTBEAT
SEQ: 210 SYS:   1 COMP:   1 MSGID:     1 | SYS_STATUS
SEQ: 211 SYS:   1 COMP:   1 MSGID:   125 | POWER_STATUS
SEQ: 212 SYS:   1 COMP:   1 MSGID:   152 | MEMINFO
SEQ: 213 SYS:   1 COMP:   1 MSGID:    62 | NAV_CONTROLLER_OUTPUT
SEQ: 214 SYS:   1 COMP:   1 MSGID:    42 | MISSION_CURRENT
SEQ: 215 SYS:   1 COMP:   1 MSGID:    24 | GPS_RAW_INT
SEQ: 216 SYS:   1 COMP:   1 MSGID:   124 | GPS2_RAW
SEQ: 217 SYS:   1 COMP:   1 MSGID:   245 | EXTENDED_SYS_STATE
SEQ: 218 SYS:   1 COMP:   1 MSGID: 11039 | MCU_STATUS
```

**Important detail:** I have sometimes seen these failing messages be received properly, very occasionally after powering on my drone, the MISSION_CURRENT message will be received over serial correctly. But if I power-cycle the drone, or kill my code that listens for MISSION_CURRENT and restarts it, then the message stops being received. I've not been able to reliably reproduce this behavior.

comments.body:
My first though is whether this could have something to do with the MAVLink dialect? I see that you're looking for `MEMINFO` but that's only part of [ardupilotmega.xml](https://github.com/ArduPilot/mavlink/blob/master/message_definitions/v1.0/ardupilotmega.xml#L1409), which actually should be included...

I will have to do some debugging, thanks for the issue anyway.

## Root Cause

After tracing through the code, the bug is in `LibmavReceiver` (the parser that feeds MavlinkDirect): it **only handles MAVLink v2** (`0xFD` magic byte). MAVLink v1 messages (`0xFE`) are silently skipped.

### How MavlinkDirect receives messages

When data arrives on a serial connection, MAVSDK runs two independent parsers on the same raw byte stream ([`serial_connection.cpp`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/cpp/src/mavsdk/core/serial_connection.cpp#L322-L335)):

1. **Standard C library parser** (`MavlinkReceiver`) — feeds MavlinkPassthrough, `intercept_incoming_messages_async`, plugins, etc. Handles both MAVLink v1 and v2.
2. **libmav `BufferParser`** (`LibmavReceiver`) — feeds MavlinkDirect. **Only handles MAVLink v2.**

In [`BufferParser::parseMessage`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/cpp/src/mavsdk/core/serial_connection.cpp), the scan literally is:

```cpp
while (start_pos < buffer_size && buffer[start_pos] != 0xFD) {
    start_pos++;  // skips 0xFE (MAVLink v1 start byte) without parsing it
}
```

Any v1 message bytes are consumed/skipped, and `nullopt` is returned — so MavlinkDirect never sees them.

### Why it works over UDP but not serial

When connecting via UDP through a GCS relay (QGC / Mission Planner), the GCS has typically negotiated MAVLink v2 with the autopilot, so all forwarded messages arrive as v2. Over a direct serial connection, ArduPilot sends many common messages as MAVLink v1 by default (HEARTBEAT, SYS_STATUS, GPS_RAW_INT, etc.). Those are exactly the ones missing.

The "sometimes works after power-on" behaviour is also consistent: if MAVSDK starts sending v2 heartbeats quickly enough, ArduPilot may switch those streams to v2 before the subscription is set up, making them visible for that session. After a power cycle, ArduPilot boots into v1 again.

The dialect question (MEMINFO in ardupilotmega.xml) is a red herring — the ardupilotmega XML *is* loaded, but that doesn't matter because the message is sent as v1 and the BufferParser never reaches the definition lookup.

### Fix

The cleanest fix is to bridge messages parsed by the standard C library into the libmav handler chain. Since the C library already handles v1+v2, every successfully parsed `mavlink_message_t` can be converted to a `Mavsdk::MavlinkMessage` (via the libmav MessageSet for field names and JSON serialization) and dispatched to `receive_libmav_message`. The independent libmav raw-stream parser could then be kept as a fallback only for custom messages loaded via `MavlinkDirect::load_custom_xml` that the C library doesn't know.

Alternatively, `BufferParser` could be extended to support MAVLink v1 (`0xFE`), but that requires converting the v1 wire format, and the C library approach is simpler and avoids duplication.

Wow, that was really really fast! I'm very glad I posted the issue here - I don't think I have all knowledge of QGC and MAVSDK required to identify this issue quickly (if at all, frankly). 

Thanks a lot for the quick fix @bansiesta!!
I hope my AI buddy is correct :). Thanks for the detailed issue.
In the meantime, you might be able to force Mavlink 2 to avoid the issue?

No problem!

I've just rolled back the core functionality I need to use `MavlinkPassthrough` for now. When I update to the next MAVSDK release I'll switch back to `MavlinkDirect` as I see `MavlinkPassthrough` is being depreciated.

issue.title: fix: add MAVLink v1 support to BufferParser

repository.name: libmavlike
repository.description: Fork of Auterion/libmav heavily changed to be used in MAVSDK

issue.body:
## Problem

`BufferParser::parseMessage` only scanned for the MAVLink v2 magic byte (`0xFD`). Any message sent as MAVLink v1 (`0xFE`) was silently dropped, because the scan loop skipped `0xFE` as noise.

This caused a real-world bug in MAVSDK: `MavlinkDirect` subscribers connected via serial never received messages that ArduPilot (and other autopilots) send as MAVLink v1 by default — `HEARTBEAT`, `SYS_STATUS`, `GPS_RAW_INT`, `MISSION_CURRENT`, etc. The same messages were received fine over UDP (where a GCS relay had already promoted them to v2) and by `MavlinkPassthrough` (which uses the standard C MAVLink parser that handles both versions). See mavlink/MAVSDK#2862.

## Changes

**`src/BufferParser.cpp`**
- `parseMessage()` now scans for either magic byte (`0xFE` or `0xFD`) and dispatches to a version-specific helper.
- `parseV1Message()` validates the v1 CRC (computed over the header and payload, skipping only the magic byte), then promotes the packet into a v2-layout `backing_memory` so that `Message::_instantiateFromMemory` can be reused without changes. Callers receive a uniform `Message` object regardless of wire version.
- `parseV2Message()` is the existing logic, extracted into a private helper.

**`include/mav/BufferParser.h`**
- Updated docstring to mention v1 support.
- Added `private` declarations for the two new helpers.

**`tests/BufferParser.cpp`**
- Added `buildV1Packet()` helper that constructs a correctly CRC'd v1 wire packet given field bytes and the message's `crcExtra`.
- New test cases:
  - Valid v1 packet parsed with correct field values and header metadata
  - Bad CRC rejected; entire packet consumed
  - Unknown message ID skipped; entire packet consumed
  - Incomplete v1 header (< 6 bytes) — returns nullopt, `bytes_consumed = 0`
  - Partial payload — returns nullopt, `bytes_consumed = 0`
  - Garbage bytes before v1 packet are skipped correctly
  - Mixed buffer: v1 then v2 parsed in sequence
  - Mixed buffer: v2 then v1 parsed in sequence

All 13 test cases pass.

issue.title: fix: bridge MAVLink v1 messages to MavlinkDirect on serial connections

repository.name: MAVSDK
repository.description: API and library for MAVLink compatible systems written in C++ 20

issue.body:
Fixes #2862.

## Root cause

`libmav`'s `BufferParser` only recognises the MAVLink v2 magic byte (`0xFD`). Any v1 frame (`0xFE`) arriving over a direct serial link was silently skipped, so `MavlinkDirect` subscribers never received HEARTBEAT, SYS_STATUS, GPS_RAW_INT and the other messages ArduPilot sends as v1 by default.

## Fix

When the standard C-library parser (`MavlinkReceiver`) successfully parses a v1 frame, re-encode it as v2 with `mavlink_msg_to_send_buffer` and feed it through `parse_message_safe` so libmav can deserialise the fields. A new `LibmavReceiver::bridge_from_mavlink_message()` method encapsulates the conversion.

The existing raw-stream libmav parser loop is unchanged — it continues to handle v2 messages and any custom-XML messages the C library does not know.

## Why UDP was unaffected

When connecting via a GCS relay (QGC / Mission Planner), the GCS has typically negotiated MAVLink v2 with the autopilot, so all forwarded UDP messages arrive as v2. Over a direct serial link ArduPilot boots into v1 and the bug manifests.

issue.title: fix: bump libmavlike to add MAVLink v1 support in BufferParser

repository.name: MAVSDK
repository.description: API and library for MAVLink compatible systems written in C++ 20

issue.body:
## Problem

Closes #2862.

`MavlinkDirect` subscribers connected over serial never received messages that ArduPilot sends as MAVLink v1 by default (HEARTBEAT, SYS_STATUS, GPS_RAW_INT, MISSION_CURRENT, etc.). The same messages were received fine over UDP (where a GCS relay re-sends them as v2) and via MavlinkPassthrough (which uses the standard C library parser that handles both v1 and v2).

Root cause: `LibmavReceiver` uses libmavlike's `BufferParser`, which previously only scanned for the MAVLink v2 magic byte (`0xFD`). MAVLink v1 packets (`0xFE`) were silently skipped.

## Fix

Bump libmavlike to [julianoes/libmavlike#2](https://github.com/julianoes/libmavlike/pull/2), which adds full MAVLink v1 support to `BufferParser`:

- `parseMessage()` now detects both magic bytes
- `parseV1Message()` validates the v1 CRC and promotes the packet into the v2 backing-memory layout so `Message::_instantiateFromMemory` can be reused — callers receive a uniform `Message` regardless of wire version
- New tests cover: valid v1 parse, bad CRC, unknown ID, partial header/payload, garbage prefix, and mixed v1+v2 buffers in both orders

timeline.body:
No problem!

I've just rolled back the core functionality I need to use `MavlinkPassthrough` for now. When I update to the next MAVSDK release I'll switch back to `MavlinkDirect` as I see `MavlinkPassthrough` is being depreciated.
